subject: maths
title: Year 10 Maths challenge
summary: A mixed challenge test covering all of Year 10 Maths: compound interest, surds, quadratics, simultaneous equations, inequalities, trigonometry, bearings, 3D shapes, statistics and probability.
body:
This is your Year 10 Maths challenge: a mixed test covering the whole year. It is harder than the practice questions in each lesson, because every question could come from any topic — just like a real end-of-year test. Use it to find out what you really know, and which lessons to go back to.

## How to use this challenge

- **Time:** 60 minutes for everything — the short-answer questions first, then the 20 multiple-choice questions below.
- **Calculator:** allowed (scientific, in degree mode).
- **Conditions:** quiet spot, no notes, phone away. Write your short-answer working on paper.
- **Marking:** check your short answers against the worked solutions. Give yourself a mark for each correct step, not just the final answer — that is how teachers mark too.
- **Scoring guide:** 80% or more — excellent, you're ready for next year. 60–79% — solid, revise the topics you dropped marks on. Under 60% — go back through the lessons for the topics you missed, then try again in a week.

## Topics covered

Number and finance (compound interest, surds, fractional indices) · Algebra (factorising and solving quadratics, parabolas, simultaneous equations, inequalities, exponential decay) · Measurement (trigonometry, bearings, angles of elevation, cones and spheres) · Space (circle properties) · Statistics and probability (box plots, scatterplots, conditional probability).

## Short-answer questions

Show all your working. Marks are in brackets.

**Question 1** (3 marks)
$5000 is invested at 4% per year, compounded annually, for 3 years. Find the final amount and the interest earned.

**Question 2** (4 marks)
a) Solve x² − 5x − 14 = 0. (2 marks)
b) Find the coordinates of the turning point of y = x² − 5x − 14. (2 marks)

**Question 3** (3 marks)
Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 11 and x − y = 1.

**Question 4** (4 marks)
A boat sails 12 km from a harbour on a bearing of 060°T. How far east and how far north of the harbour is the boat? Give answers correct to two decimal places where needed.

**Question 5** (4 marks)
Here are 8 test scores: 12, 15, 18, 22, 25, 27, 30, 41.
a) Find the five-number summary. (2 marks)
b) Find the interquartile range. (1 mark)
c) Is 41 an outlier? Use the 1.5 × IQR rule. (1 mark)

## Worked solutions

Try every question before you read these!

**Question 1**
A = P(1 + r)ⁿ = 5000 × 1.04³ = 5000 × 1.124864 = **$5624.32**
Interest = 5624.32 − 5000 = **$624.32**
(Simple interest would only give $600 — compounding earns interest on the interest.)

**Question 2**
a) Find two numbers that multiply to −14 and add to −5: −7 and 2.
(x − 7)(x + 2) = 0, so **x = 7 or x = −2** (null factor law).
b) The turning point is halfway between the x-intercepts: x = (7 + (−2)) ÷ 2 = 2.5.
y = 2.5² − 5(2.5) − 14 = 6.25 − 12.5 − 14 = −20.25
Turning point: **(2.5, −20.25)**, a minimum because the x² term is positive.

**Question 3**
Add the equations to eliminate y: (2x + y) + (x − y) = 11 + 1, so 3x = 12 and **x = 4**.
Substitute into x − y = 1: 4 − y = 1, so **y = 3**.
Check in the first equation: 2(4) + 3 = 11 ✓

**Question 4**
A bearing of 060°T is 60° clockwise from north. Draw a right-angled triangle with the 12 km path as the hypotenuse and the 60° angle at the harbour, measured from the north line.
East (opposite the 60° angle): 12 × sin 60° ≈ **10.39 km**
North (adjacent to the 60° angle): 12 × cos 60° = **6 km**

**Question 5**
a) Minimum = 12; maximum = 41.
Median = average of the 4th and 5th scores = (22 + 25) ÷ 2 = 23.5.
Q1 = median of the lower half (12, 15, 18, 22) = (15 + 18) ÷ 2 = 16.5.
Q3 = median of the upper half (25, 27, 30, 41) = (27 + 30) ÷ 2 = 28.5.
Five-number summary: **12, 16.5, 23.5, 28.5, 41**
b) IQR = 28.5 − 16.5 = **12**
c) Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5 × IQR = 28.5 + 18 = 46.5. Since 41 is below 46.5, **41 is not an outlier**.

## Challenge tips

- **Quadratics:** get everything to one side so it equals 0 *before* factorising — the null factor law only works with 0.
- **Never divide both sides by x** (as in x² = 3x). You lose the solution x = 0. Factorise instead: x(x − 3) = 0.
- **Inequalities:** multiplying or dividing by a negative number flips the sign.
- **Bearings:** start at north, turn clockwise, always use three digits (060°T, not 60°).
- **If you remember one thing:** for compound interest, the money grows by multiplying by (1 + r) every period — so A = P(1 + r)ⁿ.

questions.prompt: $2000 is invested at 6% per year, compounded monthly, for 1 year. What is the final amount, to the nearest cent?
questions.explanation: Monthly rate = 6% ÷ 12 = 0.5%, over 12 months: A = 2000 × 1.005¹² ≈ $2123.36. $2120.00 is simple interest; compounding monthly earns slightly more. $2010.00 is only one month.

questions.prompt: Simplify √50.
questions.explanation: 50 = 25 × 2 and 25 is a perfect square, so √50 = √25 × √2 = 5√2. 25√2 forgets to take the square root of 25.

questions.prompt: Evaluate 8^(2/3).
questions.explanation: The denominator 3 means cube root, the numerator 2 means square: 8^(2/3) = (∛8)² = 2² = 4. 2 stops after the cube root.

questions.prompt: Factorise x² + 2x − 15.
questions.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to −15 and add to +2: they are +5 and −3, giving (x + 5)(x − 3). (x − 5)(x + 3) has the signs swapped — it expands to x² − 2x − 15.

questions.prompt: Factorise 4x² − 25.
questions.explanation: This is a difference of two squares: (2x)² − 5² = (2x − 5)(2x + 5). (2x − 5)² would expand to 4x² − 20x + 25, which has a middle term.

questions.prompt: Solve x² = 3x.
questions.explanation: Rearrange: x² − 3x = 0, so x(x − 3) = 0, giving x = 0 or x = 3. Dividing both sides by x gives only x = 3 and loses the x = 0 solution.

questions.prompt: Solve x² − 4x + 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: It doesn't factorise, so use the quadratic formula: x = (4 ± √(16 − 4)) ÷ 2 = (4 ± √12) ÷ 2 = (4 ± 2√3) ÷ 2 = 2 ± √3. 2 ± √12 forgets to divide the square root by 2 as well.

questions.prompt: What is the turning point of y = (x − 2)² + 3?
questions.explanation: In turning-point form y = (x − h)² + k, the turning point is (h, k). Here h = 2 (the sign flips inside the bracket) and k = 3. (−2, 3) is the common trap of copying the sign straight from the bracket.

questions.prompt: How many x-intercepts does the graph of y = x² + 2x + 5 have?
questions.explanation: Use the discriminant: Δ = b² − 4ac = 4 − 20 = −16. A negative discriminant means no real solutions, so the parabola never touches the x-axis.

questions.prompt: Solve simultaneously: y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 7.
questions.explanation: Set them equal: 2x + 1 = −x + 7, so 3x = 6 and x = 2. Then y = 2(2) + 1 = 5. Check in the second equation: −2 + 7 = 5 ✓

questions.prompt: Solve −3x + 2 > 14.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2: −3x > 12. Divide by −3 and flip the inequality sign: x < −4. 'Greater than −4' forgets that dividing by a negative reverses the sign.

questions.prompt: A car bought for $30 000 loses 15% of its value each year. What is it worth after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.85: 30 000 × 0.85² = $21 675. $21 000 takes 15% of the original price off twice (simple depreciation), but the second year's 15% is taken from the lower value.

questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite angle θ is 7 cm and the adjacent side is 10 cm. Find θ to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Opposite and adjacent → tan: θ = tan⁻¹(7/10) ≈ 35.0°. 44.4° uses sin⁻¹ by mistake, and 55.0° is the other acute angle in the triangle.

questions.prompt: From a point 50 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is 32°. How tall is the tower, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The height is opposite the 32° angle and the 50 m is adjacent: h = 50 × tan 32° ≈ 31.24 m. 26.50 m uses sine and 42.40 m uses cosine instead of tangent.

questions.prompt: The bearing of B from A is 050°T. What is the bearing of A from B?
questions.explanation: A back bearing differs by 180°: 50° + 180° = 230°T. 130°T is 180° − 50°, which is a different direction altogether.

questions.prompt: Find the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 8 cm, to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: V = ⅓πr²h = ⅓ × π × 9 × 8 = 24π ≈ 75.4 cm³. 226.2 cm³ is the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height — a cone is exactly one third of that.

questions.prompt: Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 5 cm, to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: SA = 4πr² = 4 × π × 25 = 100π ≈ 314.2 cm². 78.5 cm² is just πr² (one circle), and 523.6 is the volume (⁴⁄₃πr³).

questions.prompt: Points A and B lie on a circle with centre O. Point C is also on the circle. If angle ACB at the circumference is 35°, what is angle AOB at the centre?
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc: 2 × 35° = 70°. 17.5° halves it instead of doubling.

questions.prompt: A scatterplot has a correlation coefficient of r = −0.85. Which description fits best?
questions.explanation: The sign shows direction (negative: as one goes up, the other goes down), and a size near 1 shows strength. 0.85 is strong. Remember: correlation alone never proves that one variable causes the other.

questions.prompt: In a group of 60 students, 24 play sport, and 18 of those also play music. A student is chosen at random from those who play sport. What is the probability they play music?
questions.explanation: This is conditional probability: given they play sport, the sample space shrinks to the 24 sport players. P(music | sport) = 18/24 = 3/4. 3/10 (18/60) divides by everyone instead of just the sport players.
